Subject: Quick recap + procurement questions (post-demo)

Hi Samantha — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same view: 

What we covered
- Live demo of Dedicated vs Hosted routing and the autoscale behavior for seasonal traffic
- Pricing model overview (usage + reserved commit for Dedicated)
- Data handling: VPC option and audit logs for Private deployments

Open questions specific to procurement you mentioned:
1) AP policy: PO required for amounts over your threshold?
2) Vendor onboarding: any specific forms or vendor portal requirements (W-9, insured docs)?
3) Payment methods: whether corporate card is allowed vs PO/invoice net terms.

Suggested next steps
- If PO + vendor portal required: can you share the onboarding checklist and the typical lead time?
- If card is acceptable for initial pilots, we can scope a pilot order under $2k to expedite start.
- I attached a one‑page commercial summary and a draft MUP terms doc for your procurement team to review.

Would you be able to confirm the AP rules and whether Beta Retail would consider a card-first pilot? If it helps, we can loop in our finance lead (Laura) to discuss invoices and contract language.

Thanks — Ben

Subject: Re: Quick recap + procurement questions (post-demo)

Thanks Ben — good call yesterday. I checked with AP and legal; here's the short version: 

AP / Procurement constraints (Beta Retail)
- PO is required for vendor invoices > $5,000. Below $5k, finance prefers card payments to avoid PO overhead.
- New vendor setup requires: completed vendor registration in our portal, W-9, bank details for ACH, and a vendor contact in our system. Lead time: typically 7–10 business days once paperwork is complete.
- We can consider a card payment for a pilot under $2k to get initial integration telemetry, but corporate card policy requires a pre-approved budget owner to sign off (I'll handle sign-off if we keep it under marketing/dev ops).
- Marketplace (we use AWS Marketplace for some software) is attractive because procurement can often be simplified there, but it adds a 10–12% marketplace fee.

I'll attach our vendor setup checklist (PDF) — sending to AP to confirm any additional items. If you'd like, we can do a short sync with my AP lead and your finance contact to walk through the vendor form.

Samantha
Head of Product Ops | Beta Retail
samantha.ortiz@beta-retail.com | +1 212-555-0110

Attachment: beta-vendor-checklist.pdf

Thanks for the clarity, Samantha — that helps a lot. Couple quick notes from our side and a proposed mutual action plan: 

Notes
- PO threshold makes sense. For a fast pilot we can: 
  a) do a card-first pilot under $2k (you sign off as budget owner) to validate integration and metrics, then move to PO for broader rollout; or
  b) start vendor onboarding in parallel so production rollouts can use PO/ACH once approved.
- Marketplace: we can list Redwood on AWS Marketplace (we already have a few customers there). If Beta prefers that path I can pull expected fees vs time-to-live tradeoffs — it usually reduces procurement friction but increases cost.

Proposed next steps / owners
- Ben: send an itemized pilot quote that fits under $2k for initial 30-day evaluation (today EOD).
- Samantha: share vendor registration link and point person at AP (you mentioned you would include AP on the thread).
- Marissa (cc): if AP requires any special contract language or billing contact info, could you provide the account billing profile and W-9?
- Laura (cc): happy to jump on a 20-min call with AP if they'd prefer a live walkthrough.

If that plan sounds good I can get the pilot quote over and we can aim to have the test in the next 7–10 business days.

Best — Ben

--
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi all — this is Rachel from AP. Quick confirmation from our side: 

- Confirmed: PO required for invoices > $5,000. Standard net-30 terms once vendor is onboarded.
- Vendor onboarding form received (Samantha — thanks). Required items we saw: W-9, ACH remit info, signed master services agreement (we accept MSA or a marketplace contract), and company insurance certificate for vendors that run production workloads (we can accept evidence of cloud provider shared responsibility for SaaS).
- If Redwood is willing to issue an invoice for a short pilot we will process a PO once vendor profile is created; otherwise card payment under $2k is acceptable to expedite.

We can set a 20-minute call today at 11:30am ET to walk through the vendor portal and required attachments. Please confirm and I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Rachel (AP Team)
